dashboard-view.intro: The page you open first every day: announcements, punch buttons, your personal profile, and any attendance exceptions the system found.
steps: Tap "Punch In" when you arrive and "Punch Out" before you leave; both the time and your GPS location are recorded.
On a split shift, punch out before your break and punch in when you come back; up to three pairs a day.

Besides the buttons, you can punch by typing in LINE or by scanning the QR code on the company tablet (LINE's own QR scanner works best). If you scan with the phone camera and that browser is not logged in yet, you are taken to LINE login and the punch is recorded right after.
If your phone supports fingerprint or face recognition, tap "Set up biometrics" once to pair it, then punch with biometrics from then on.
If you forgot to punch or the time is wrong, submit a make-up punch request with a reason and wait for the administrator's approval.
Fill in your ID number, address, phone and birthday under "My profile" - payroll and insurance work needs them.
Under "My Basic Information", enter your full name first — punch records and reports show this name instead of your LINE name.
notes: Punching requires location permission; if the browser blocks it, the punch fails or is recorded as an exception.
"Attendance exceptions" are detected automatically (missing punch, late, early leave). An approved make-up punch clears the exception.
Announcements are sorted by importance; red ones are important, please read them.
The QR codes on the tablet change every 30 seconds, so photos of them or copies sent to others stop working. Scan them in person.

You cannot do the same punch twice in a row; if the order is wrong, the system tells you which punch comes next. If you forget the break punches, attendance issues shows "Add break start / Add break end" buttons.
If LINE is not available, ask an admin for a login link and open it on your own phone. After that you can punch and scan the tablet QR code without LINE.
terms: Biometric punch
Pairs this phone with your account so fingerprint or face recognition replaces the punch button. Location is still recorded.
Make-up punch
A punch entered after the fact; it only enters the attendance record once an administrator approves it.

monthly-view.intro: See your whole month on a calendar: which days were normal, which had exceptions, and how much overtime you worked.
steps: The four figures on top are this month's statistics; the calendar below colors each day by status.
Use "<" and ">" to change month; tap a day to list all punch records for that day.
If a day's record is wrong, submit a make-up punch request right from that day's card.
notes: Statistics are calculated live: refresh after a make-up punch or leave request is approved and the numbers update.
You only see your own records; supervisors and administrators see company-wide data.
terms: Exception days
Days flagged for a missing punch-in or punch-out, lateness, early leave and so on.
Normal days
Days with both punches recorded at times that match your shift.

location-view.intro: Check the location your phone is currently reporting - useful before punching if you are unsure the position is accurate.
steps: Allow the browser to read your location; the map marks your current coordinates.
Compare "Status" and "Coordinates" to confirm you are inside the office or work site area.
If the position is clearly off, move near a window or outdoors, turn on GPS, and refresh.
notes: Indoors or on Wi-Fi only, the error can reach several hundred meters - that is normal.
If a punch is rejected as out of range, check this page first, then report it to the administrator.

shift-view.intro: See your shift for today and the days ahead; editing shifts happens in shift management.
steps: "Today's shift" shows today's shift type, working hours and location.
To add, adjust or batch-assign shifts, tap "Enter shift management" for the full page.
notes: Regular employees can only view their own shifts; changes are made by administrators.
Shifts drive the late/early-leave rules, so report a wrong shift as soon as you spot it.

overtime-view.intro: Apply for overtime and track approval; approved hours feed into payroll.
steps: Pick the overtime date and enter start and end times - the hours are calculated for you.
Explain the reason in the reason field (the more specific the better) and submit.
Check each request's status - pending, approved or rejected - under "Overtime records".
notes: Apply in advance or the same day where possible; requests filed long after the fact may be rejected.
Approved overtime cannot be edited or deleted by you - ask an administrator for corrections.
Hours are converted into overtime pay or compensatory leave using the statutory rates.
terms: Overtime hours
End time minus start time, with no break deducted - subtract your break yourself before entering.
Compensatory leave
Overtime hours converted into leave hours, used later as "Compensatory leave" on the leave page.

leave-view.intro: Check your remaining hours per leave type, submit leave requests, and track their progress.
steps: Look at "Leave balance" first to confirm how many hours of that type are left.
Choose the leave type, dates and times - the hours are calculated - then write the reason.
Track the status under "Leave records"; a request still pending can be cancelled and resubmitted.
notes: Annual and compensatory leave are capped by your balance; requests above the balance cannot be submitted.
Sick, bereavement and marriage leave may require supporting documents under company policy.
If you are already scheduled during the leave, confirm cover with your supervisor after approval.
terms: Annual leave
Yearly paid leave granted by length of service; unused days are handled per company policy.
Compensatory leave
Leave earned from approved overtime hours, available until used up.

salary-view.intro: The entry point for payroll; the actual payslips, settings and calculations live in the payroll system.
steps: Tap "Enter payroll system" to open the full payroll page.
Employees can view their own payslips; administrators additionally see settings and calculation tools.
notes: Payroll data is confidential - avoid leaving this page open in public or on shared devices.
If an amount looks wrong, compare it with your attendance and overtime records before contacting the administrator.

worklog-view.intro: Record a daily work log: what you did and how many hours it took.
steps: Pick the date and enter the hours worked (decimals allowed, e.g. 8.5).
Describe the day's work in at least 10 characters - be specific.
After submitting, review past logs and their approval status in the records section below.
notes: One log per day as a rule; a duplicate entry will overwrite the first or be returned.
Logged hours are entered by you and tracked separately from punch hours; the two need not match.

expense-view.intro: Request an advance (money borrowed from the company up front) or a reimbursement (paying you back for something you paid, with a receipt), and follow each request's review result.
steps: Choose the type — "Advance" or "Reimbursement" — then enter the date, amount and reason.
For a reimbursement you can add the invoice number and attach a photo of the receipt; you can also upload it later from the list below.
Press "Submit request". It appears under "My expense requests" as "Pending".
After an admin reviews it, the status changes to "Approved" or "Rejected"; a rejection comes with a reason.
notes: Amounts are in whole dollars and cannot be edited after submitting. If you made a mistake, ask an admin to reject it and submit again.
Approved advances and reimbursements are not added to or deducted from your salary automatically; payment and repayment follow company rules.
Only you and admins can see your receipt photos.
terms: Advance
Money borrowed from the company up front, paid back or deducted from salary according to company rules.
Reimbursement
Claiming back a company expense you paid yourself, with an invoice or receipt.

admin-view.intro: Administrators only: announcements, approvals, punch locations, attendance analysis and report exports all live here.
steps: Working Hours Settings adjusts the company-wide start, end and lunch times — leave hours are counted against that window.
Publish announcements under "Announcement management"; set priority to "Important" so staff see it first.
Handle make-up punch and virtual card requests under "Pending requests"; overtime, leave and work logs have their own approval sections.
Add or adjust the allowed punch coordinates and radius under "Punch locations" - this directly decides whether staff can punch.
"Attendance analysis" shows overall hours and punch-time distribution; the report section exports Excel for HR or accounting.
"Pending expense requests" is where you review employees' advances and reimbursements; open the attachments to see receipt photos.

Under "Punch kiosk", enter a location name and create a link. Open it on a company tablet and leave it on — it keeps showing refreshing clock-in and clock-out QR codes. "QR code punch" creates a one-off QR code instead.
"Activity log" lets you search by month, action and keyword to see who changed reviews, roles, employees, shifts or salary settings, and when.
"Edit name" under employee management changes an employee's LINE name to their real name.

"Employee management": for staff who cannot use LINE, press "Login link" to create a link or QR code they open on their own phone to log in; add new staff without LINE with "Add employee (no LINE)". Each link works once; if it goes to the wrong person, create a new one and the old one stops working.
notes: Approvals affect attendance and payroll immediately; when rejecting, state the reason so the employee knows how to fix it.
Too small a radius blocks legitimate punches; too large defeats the purpose of location control.
Exported files contain personal and salary data - do not forward them outside the company.
After changing the working hours, only leave submitted afterwards uses the new figures; approved leave is not recalculated.

The kiosk link works like a key for the tablet, so do not send it to employees. If the tablet is lost or the link leaks, create a new link or press "Disable kiosk" and the old one stops working immediately.
The activity log is read-only; ID numbers and bank accounts are masked in it.
terms: Virtual card
An alternative punch method approved by an administrator when location punching is unavailable.
Punch radius
The distance in meters around the configured coordinates within which punching is allowed.
Punch kiosk
A company tablet that keeps showing QR codes, refreshed every 30 seconds. Staff scan them on site to punch, no GPS needed.
Activity log
An automatic history of admin actions, so you can check who did what and when if there is a dispute.

view-tab.intro: Review the shifts assigned over a chosen period and confirm who works which shift each day.
steps: Pick a month or date range and search; the table lists every shift in that period.
To change one shift, edit that row directly, or delete it and add it again.
notes: Shift changes affect late/early-leave rules and payroll, so finish adjustments before the shift day.

add-tab.intro: Add one shift at a time: pick the employee, date, shift and location.
steps: Choose the employee and date, then a shift. Start, end and break minutes are filled in from the shift settings, and the hours for that shift appear under the form.
For a split shift (e.g. 10:30–21:30), just pick that shift; the gap in the middle is already its break minutes.
To adjust just this one, change the times or break minutes directly.

After choosing the employee and date, the shifts they already have that day are listed under the form. If you scheduled one twice by mistake, press "Delete" on that row, or "Edit" and then "Delete this shift".
Check the location and submit, then confirm it appears under "View Shifts".
notes: On split shifts staff punch out before the break and in when they return (up to three pairs a day); hours follow the actual punches, to the minute. If the break punches are missing, the shift's break minutes are deducted and the day shows up under attendance issues.
On days with no shift, 1 hour is taken off only when someone is on site for more than 8 hours.
The same shift for the same person on the same day is rejected, so check the day first.

batch-tab.intro: Upload a CSV or Excel file to add many shifts at once, e.g. next month's rota.
steps: Press "Download Template" and fill in the columns: employee ID, name, date, shift, start, end, location, note, break minutes.
You can enter just the shift code (e.g. E); blank times and break minutes come from the shift settings. Fill them in to adjust a single row.
Pick the file, check the preview (shift names and times), then press "Confirm Upload".
Spot-check a few days under "View Shifts" afterwards.
notes: Copy employee IDs from employee management on the admin page; rows with a wrong ID fail.
A shift that already exists for the same person, day and shift is skipped and listed in the result.
Public holidays and approved leave are not skipped automatically; check and adjust them yourself.

templates-tab.intro: Manage the shop's shifts: code, name, planned start and end, and break minutes. Picking a shift when scheduling fills these in.
steps: Each row is a shift. Enter the code (e.g. E), name, times and break minutes; total minutes and work hours are calculated for you.
For a split shift, put the gap in "Break (min)", e.g. 10:30–21:30 with a 180-minute break is 8 work hours.
Tick "Overnight" for shifts ending after midnight. Untick "Active" for shifts you no longer use instead of deleting them.
Press "Save shift settings" when done.
notes: Only admins can change these: break minutes directly affect hourly staff's hours and pay.
Changes only apply to shifts scheduled afterwards; shifts already scheduled (or paid) stay as they were.
Codes must be unique. Day-off shifts such as leave can be left without times.
terms: Break (min)
Unpaid time in the middle of a shift, taken off the hours worked.
Overnight
The shift ends the next day, e.g. 20:00 to 02:00.

stats-tab.intro: Statistics for the roster: how many days each person is scheduled and whether shift types are evenly spread.
steps: Pick the period and search; the chart and table update together.
If someone has clearly too many or too few shifts, go back to batch scheduling to rebalance.
notes: Only scheduled shifts are counted, not actual attendance - see the attendance records for that.

employee-salary.intro: Employees view their own payslip: base pay, allowances, overtime pay and deductions.
steps: Pick the year and month to list that month's payslip details.
If an amount looks wrong, compare it with the same month's attendance and overtime records before contacting the administrator.
notes: Salary data is confidential - avoid opening or screenshotting it on shared devices.
The bottom of the payslip shows whether you earned the attendance bonus this month and why, plus any note from the admin.

salary-setting.intro: Set the pay rules and each employee's pay conditions. Company-wide rules are at the top; below, pick a person on the left and fill in their conditions on the right.
steps: Company-wide settings let you define custom allowances and deductions, and adjust overtime rates and insurance brackets.
"Payroll rules" set the amounts and thresholds for the attendance bonus, meal pay and birthday gift. Full-time = "monthly" salary type, part-time = "hourly".
Once custom items are defined, a matching amount field appears at the bottom of every employee's form.
Pick an employee from the searchable list on the left, then set salary type, base amount, allowances and deductions, and save.
notes: Settings apply to future calculations, so check which month they take effect from; existing payslips are not recalculated.
Fill in insurance brackets from the official published table — wrong figures mean wrong deductions.
Do not change a custom item's code once set; a changed code is a new item and the amounts already entered no longer match it.
Deleting a custom item only stops it counting toward pay. The amounts stay on file and come back if you add it again.

Full-time attendance bonus: one late arrival within 5 minutes and 2 missed punches are allowed per month; being more than 5 minutes late, personal/sick/hospital leave or an unexcused absence cancels it (the numbers are adjustable).

Meal pay: days with 8+ hours (actual hours for full-time, scheduled hours for part-time) × NT$110. The birthday gift needs a birthday this month and 3+ months of employment (hire date from the salary settings).
Overtime hourly rate for monthly staff = (base + meal allowance + position allowance) ÷ 30 ÷ 8. The multipliers default to the Labor Standards Act and can be changed under overtime rates.
terms: Monthly pay
A fixed monthly salary; leave and absence are deducted pro rata from the daily rate.
Hourly pay
Paid on actual hours worked, taken from the punch records.
Insurance bracket
The salary band used to work out labor and health insurance, matched against the official published table.
Attendance bonus note
Each payslip says whether the bonus was earned and why not (e.g. "late more than 5 minutes once").

bonus-records.intro: Records of the three-festival bonuses: how much was paid for Dragon Boat, Mid-Autumn and Lunar New Year.
steps: Pick a year to see that year's bonus records.
Administrators can add or adjust amounts; employees only see their own.
notes: Festival bonuses are not part of regular salary calculation but are still income and appear in annual income data.

salary-calc.intro: Calculate one employee's pay for one month. Just pick the person and the month; the monthly or hourly formula is chosen from their salary type.
steps: Pick the employee and the month. The hint below shows whether they are monthly or hourly paid.
Press Start calculation and review the result: attendance, overtime and deductions.
Save it as an official payslip once it checks out. To run the whole company at once, use the batch calculation in Salary Reports.
After calculating, fill in the sales bonus, advance repayment, manual items and a note under "Payslip adjustments", then press "Save and recalculate".
notes: Approve every punch correction, overtime and leave request for that month first, or the result will come out short.
Recalculating the same month overwrites the previous result.
Missing punches make hourly staff's hours too low, so clear the punch-correction queue first.
Leave the advance blank to use this month's approved advance requests; leave the attendance bonus blank to follow the payroll rules, or enter an amount to override.
Adjustments are kept on the payslip and reused on every recalculation, including when the employee opens their own payslip.
terms: Monthly pay
A fixed monthly salary; leave and absence are deducted pro rata from the daily rate.
Hourly pay
Paid on actual hours worked, taken from the punch records.

salary-report.intro: Look up payslips that have been generated, plus two time-savers: batch calculation and settings copy.
steps: Pick a month and load the list to see each employee's gross, deductions and net pay; you can export the report from here.
Batch calculate salaries runs every active employee for that month and saves the results, in chunks if the team is large.
Copy salary settings applies one employee's setup to others — handy for new hires or a company-wide raise.
notes: Do not delete payslips that have already been paid out; make a correcting adjustment and leave a record instead.
Batch calculation overwrites existing payslips for that month, so finish all approvals first.
Copying settings carries pay conditions only; personal data such as ID number, bank account and hire date is never copied.
Exported files contain personal and salary data — do not send them outside the company.
